AirJoule Says It Can Generate Water From Heat. Now It Is Buying to Scale Up. — Interview
By Kimberley Kao
AirJoule Technologies is making its first acquisition to advance its technology for artificial-intelligence data centers, as it seeks to commercialize its water technology.
The atmospheric water-generation company is buying BitSink for $27 million, with as much as an additional $40 million tied to revenue milestones for the startup, AirJoule said Monday.
South Carolina-based BitSink designs and deploys cooling, electrical distribution and modular infrastructure for AI and high-density computing, including cryptocurrency mining data centers.

The additional consideration of $40 million requires BitSink to hit $157 million in cumulative revenue over three years, beginning with $30 million in 2027 and $63 million in 2028, AirJoule Chief Financial Officer Stephen Pang said in an interview.
BitSink's operations and financial results will be consolidated into AirJoule's statements from the third quarter, Pang said.
Shares of Nasdaq-listed AirJoule, which has a joint venture with GE Vernova, have risen more than 30% over the past six months.
The company said its technology is designed to convert low-grade waste heat into usable water.
"Data centers are now the largest near-term opportunity," said Matt Jore, founder and chief executive of AirJoule, in an interview.
The company plans to deploy its heat-to-water technology at an operating European data center in the fourth quarter to demonstrate its technology on a commercial scale, Jore said.

AirJoule is also active in other sectors. It is working with the U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center on military applications, and deploying pilot systems for water-constrained residential development in the U.S., he added.
The company might evaluate future merger and acquisition opportunities that "strengthen our cooling, power, water or manufacturing capabilities," Jore said, without naming any targets.
"Over time, BitSink gives us a foundation from which to pursue both organic growth and selective strategic expansion in AI infrastructure," he said.
